title: Keritot 14
description: How Rabbi Meir lets one prohibition fall on another when it is inclusive or expanded, why the mishna counts four sin offerings for one olive-bulk and not five or six, Rafram’s statement on carrying on Yom Kippur, and the mishnayot on a single act of intercourse that incurs six or seven sin offerings, with Rabbi Yosei’s father’s wife and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri’s mother-in-law.

🌴 A date-bulk on Yom Kippur: a kidney with its fat, or dates to fill it out
🐐 The scapegoat “even on Shabbat” and Rafram’s statement, declared an error
⚖️ One act of intercourse, six sin offerings: how each prohibition is added
📜 Rabbi Yosei: the elder who transgressed, levirate marriage and secondary relatives
👵 Mother-in-law and her mother: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and “one category”

a1.he: גְּמָ׳ נֵימָא אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר? נְהִי דְּאִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר לֵית לֵיהּ, אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל וְאִיסּוּר מוֹסִיף אִית לֵיהּ.

a2.he: טָהוֹר, מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא אֲסִיר אֶלָּא בְּחֵלֶב, הֲוָה לֵיהּ טָמֵא, מִיגּוֹ דַּאֲסִיר בַּחֲתִיכוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת – אִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ נָמֵי אִיסּוּרָא עִילָּוֵי חֵלֶב.

a3.he: וְחֵלֶב מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא אֲסִיר אֶלָּא בַּאֲכִילָה, אַקְדְּשֵׁיהּ, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ אִיסּוּרָא דַּהֲנָאָה – אִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ לְגַבֵּי חֵלֶב.

a4.he: וְאַכַּתִּי לְהֶדְיוֹט הוּא דַּאֲסִיר אֲבָל לְגָבוֹהַּ שְׁרֵי, הֲוָה לֵיהּ נוֹתָר, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּרָא לְגַבֵּי גָּבוֹהַּ – אִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ לְגַבֵּי הֶדְיוֹט. חָל עֲלֵיהּ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ אִיסּוּר לְגַבֵּי חוּלִּין – אִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ לְגַבֵּי גָבוֹהַּ.

a5.he: וְנִתְנֵי: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת, וְנוֹקְמַהּ כְּגוֹן דַּאֲכַל כְּזַיִת פִּיגּוּל! בַּחֲדָא בְּהֵמָה קָמַיְירֵי, בִּשְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת לָא קָמַיְירֵי, וְנוֹתָר וּפִיגּוּל בַּחֲדָא בְּהֵמָה לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ.

a6.he: אַלְּמָה לָא? מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱלָה אֵבֶר פִּיגּוּל לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, דְּפָקַע פִּיגּוּלֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ נוֹתָר,

a7.he: וְכִדְאָמַר עוּלָּא: קוֹמֶץ פִּיגּוּל שֶׁהֶעֱלָה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ – פָּקַע פִּיגּוּלוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ נוֹתָר. בְּאֵבֶר אֶחָד קָא מַיְירֵי, בִּשְׁנֵי אֵבָרִים לָא קָמַיְירֵי, וְנוֹתָר וּפִיגּוּל בְּחַד אֵבֶר לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ.

a8.he: אַלְּמָה לָא? מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱלָה אֵבֶר פִּיגּוּל לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, דְּפַלְגֵיהּ אַנְּחֵיהּ עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, וּפַלְגֵיהּ מֵאַבָּרַאי דְּמִזְבֵּחַ, דְּהָהוּא דְּמִזְבֵּחַ פָּקַע פִּיגּוּל וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ נוֹתָר, וְכִדְאָמַר עוּלָּא: קוֹמֶץ פִּיגּוּל שֶׁהֶעֱלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ – פָּקַע פִּיגּוּלוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וְהָוֵי לֵיהּ נוֹתָר!

a9.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, אִי רוּבָּא דְּמִזְבֵּחַ – שִׁדְיֵיהּ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ, רוּבָּא דְּבָרַאי – שִׁדְיֵיהּ לְבָרַאי.

a10.he: תִּפְשׁוֹט דְּבָעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הָלְכוּ בְּאֵבָרִים אַחַר הָרוֹב אוֹ לֹא! אֶלָּא, בִּכְזַיִת אֶחָד קָמַיְירֵי, בִּשְׁנֵי זֵיתִים לָא קָא מַיְירֵי.

a11.he: וְלָא? וְהָקָתָנֵי ״יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים״, וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כּוֹתֶבֶת [הוּא] דְּמִחַיַּיב, וְכוֹתֶבֶת אִית בַּיהּ שְׁנֵי זֵיתִים!

a12.he: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל כּוּלְיָא בְּחֶלְבָּהּ. רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּמַלְּיֵיהּ בְּתַמְרֵי.

a13.he: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַחָא מַתְנֵי ״חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת״, וּמְתָרֵיץ לַהּ: כְּגוֹן דַּאֲכַל כְּזַיִת פִּיגּוּל, וְלָא מְשַׁנֵּי כְּהָנֵי שִׁינּוּיֵי דְּקָא מְשַׁנֵּינַן.

a14.he: וְנִתְנֵי: ״שֵׁשׁ חַטָּאוֹת״, וְנוֹקְמַהּ כְּגוֹן דַּאֲכַל כְּזַיִת דָּם! בַּחֲדָא אֲכִילָה קָא מַיְירֵי, בִּשְׁתֵּי אֲכִילוֹת לֹא קָא מַיְירֵי, וְשִׁיעֲרוּ חֲכָמִים דְּאֵין בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה מַחֲזִיק יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁנֵי זֵיתִים.

a15.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳. וְנִתְנֵי: ״אִם הוֹצִיאוֹ – חַיָּיב״, מַאי טַעְמָא קָתָנֵי ״אִם הָיְתָה שַׁבָּת״? אָמַר רַפְרָם: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת: עֵירוּב וְהוֹצָאָה לְשַׁבָּת, וְאֵין עֵירוּב וְהוֹצָאָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.

a16.he: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא יֵשׁ עֵירוּב וְהוֹצָאָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: אִם הָיְתָה שַׁבָּת וְהוֹצִיאוֹ – חַיָּיב אַף מִשּׁוּם שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים!

a17.he: אֶלָּא אִי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַפְרָם עַל הָדָא אִיתְּמַר, דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְשִׁלַּח בְּיַד אִישׁ עִתִּי״, ״אִישׁ״ – לְהַכְשִׁיר אֶת הַזָּר. ״עִתִּי״ – אֲפִילּוּ בְּטוּמְאָה וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת, ״עִתִּי״ – בִּמְזוּמָּן.

a18.he: קָתָנֵי: ״עִתִּי״ – אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת, אָמַר רַפְרָם: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת עֵירוּב וְהוֹצָאָה לְשַׁבָּת, וְאֵין עֵירוּב וְהוֹצָאָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.

a19.he: מִמַּאי? שָׁאנֵי שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ, דְּהֶכְשֵׁירוֹ בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים בְּכָךְ! אֶלָּא דְּרַפְרָם בְּרוּתָא הִיא.

a20.he: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ בָּא בִּיאָה אַחַת וְחַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ שֵׁשׁ חַטָּאוֹת, כֵּיצַד? הַבָּא עַל בִּתּוֹ חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם בִּתּוֹ, וַאֲחוֹתוֹ, אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו, וְאֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אָבִיו, וְאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, וְנִדָּה.

b1.he: גְּמָ׳ וְהָא לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר! נְהִי דְּאִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר לֵית לֵיהּ, אִיסּוּר מוֹסִיף וְאִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל אִית לֵיהּ.

b2.he: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּא עַל אִמּוֹ וְהוֹלִיד בַּת, דְּאִיסּוּר בִּתּוֹ וַאֲחוֹתוֹ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי אָתֵי. נִשֵּׂאת לְאָחִיו, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּר לְגַבֵּי אַחִין – אִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּרָא לְגַבֵּי דִּידֵיהּ.

b3.he: נִשֵּׂאת לַאֲחִי אָבִיו, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּרָא לְגַבֵּי שְׁאָר אֲחֵי אָבִיו – אִיתּוֹסַף לְגַבֵּי דִּידֵיהּ. הָוְיָא לַהּ אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּר לְגַבֵּי עָלְמָא – אִיתּוֹסַף נָמֵי לְגַבֵּי דִּידֵיהּ. הָוְיָא לַהּ נִדָּה, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּר לְגַבֵּי בַּעֲלַהּ – אִיתּוֹסַף נָמֵי לְגַבֵּי דִּידֵיהּ.

b4.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַבָּא עַל בַּת בִּתּוֹ – חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם בַּת בִּתּוֹ, וְכַלָּתוֹ, וְאֵשֶׁת אָחִיו, וְאֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אָבִיו, וַאֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, וְנִדָּה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִם עָבַר זָקֵן וּנְשָׂאָהּ – חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָב.

b5.he: וְכֵן הַבָּא עַל בַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְעַל בַּת בִּתָּהּ.

b6.he: גְּמָ׳ קָתָנֵי: חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָב. מִי שַׁרְיָא לֵיהּ? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּפְלָה לוֹ לְיִבּוּם.

b7.he: אִי הָכִי, מַאי ״עָבַר״? אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: שֶׁעָבַר מִשּׁוּם כַּלַּת בְּנוֹ, שְׁנִיָּה.

b8.he: כִּדְתַנְיָא: כַּלָּתוֹ עֶרְוָה, כַּלַּת בְּנוֹ שְׁנִיָּה. וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא בְּבַת בְּנוֹ, וּבְבַת בֶּן בְּנוֹ. עַד סוֹף כׇּל הַדּוֹרוֹת.

b9.he: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר? וְהָא תְנַן: עָבַר עֲבֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת – נִידּוֹן בַּחֲמוּרָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נִידּוֹן בְּזִיקָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁבָּאָה עָלָיו.

b10.he: וְתַנְיָא: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נִידּוֹן בְּזִיקָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה? חֲמוֹתוֹ וְנַעֲשֵׂת אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ – נִידּוֹן מִשּׁוּם חֲמוֹתוֹ.

b11.he: אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ וְנַעֲשֵׂת חֲמוֹתוֹ – נִידּוֹן מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ!

b12.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאִיסּוּר מוֹסִיף. וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאִיסּוּר מוֹסִיף.

b13.he: מַאי אִיסּוּר מוֹסִיף אִיכָּא הָכָא? דְּאִיכָּא בְּרָא לְסָבָא, מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּרָא לְגַבֵּי בְּרֵיהּ – אִיתּוֹסַף אִיסּוּרָא לְגַבֵּי דִּידֵיהּ.

b14.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַבָּא עַל חֲמוֹתוֹ חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם חֲמוֹתוֹ, וְכַלָּתוֹ, וְאֵשֶׁת אָחִיו, וְאֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אָבִיו, וַאֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, וְנִדָּה. וְכֵן הַבָּא עַל אֵם חָמִיו, וְעַל אֵם חֲמוֹתוֹ.

b15.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: הַבָּא עַל חֲמוֹתוֹ חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם חֲמוֹתוֹ, וְאֵם חֲמוֹתוֹ, וְאֵם חָמִיו. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שְׁלׇשְׁתָּן שֵׁם אֶחָד הֵן.

b16.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וְסוֹמְכוֹס אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן. סוֹמְכוֹס מַאי הִיא? דִּתְנַן:

messages.text: Continued from 13b: the mishna taught that one who is impure and eats forbidden fat that was left over [notar] from a consecrated offering, on Yom Kippur, is liable to four sin offerings and one guilt offering. Rabbi Meir added that if it was Shabbat and he carried it out, he is liable; the Rabbis said that is not from the same type.
Gemara
Let us say that it is evident from the mishna that Rabbi Meir holds that a prohibition takes effect where another prohibition already exists.

Although he does not generally hold that a prohibition takes effect where another prohibition already exists, with regard to a more inclusive prohibition and an expanded prohibition, he holds that the second prohibition does take effect where a prohibition already exists. Under certain circumstances a second prohibition takes effect, and under other circumstances it does not. When the second prohibition is an expanded or inclusive prohibition, it takes effect.

notes.he: גרידא חל על איסור לית ליה כגון האוכל נבלת בהמה טמאה אינו חייב משום נבלה דהיינו איסור גרידא דליכא לא כולל ולא מוסיף:
notes.en: Gemara. Granted that a mere prohibition taking effect on a prohibition he does not hold: for example, one who eats the carcass of a non-kosher animal is not liable on account of a carcass [nevela], since that is a mere prohibition, neither inclusive nor expanded.

notes.he: גרידא לית ליה כגון היכא דאמר שבועה שלא אוכל חלב ואכל דאינו חייב אלא משום חלב ולא משום שבועה ואין איסור חל על איסור. וכן נזיר שאמר שבועה שלא אוכל ענבים ואכל אבל במקום איסור מוסיף היכא דנתוספו אחרים על איסורו או באיסור כולל היכא דכולל דברים המותרים עם דברים האסורין כגון נזיר שאמר שלא אוכל תאנים וענבים ואכל תאנים וענבים מיגו דחלה (על) איסור שבועה אתאנים חלה נמי אענבים. והכי נמי כל היכא דאיכא איסור מוסיף או איסור כולל אית ליה איסור חל על איסור. והכא נמי טהור מעיקרא לא אסיר אלא בחלב אבל בקדשים קלים או אם היה כהן בקדשי קדשים מצי אכיל:
notes.en: [A printer’s marker at the start reads: “Up to here belongs to 13b.”] Granted that a prohibition taking effect on a prohibition, a mere one, he does not hold: for example, where one said, “An oath that I will not eat forbidden fat,” and ate it, he is liable only on account of the fat and not on account of the oath, and a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition. And similarly a nazirite who said, “An oath that I will not eat grapes,” and ate. But where there is an expanded prohibition, where others were added to his prohibition, or an inclusive prohibition, where it includes permitted things together with forbidden things, for example a nazirite who said, “[An oath] that I will not eat figs and grapes,” and ate figs and grapes: since the prohibition of the oath took effect on the figs, it takes effect on the grapes as well. So too, wherever there is an expanded or an inclusive prohibition, he holds that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition. And here too, a pure person was initially forbidden only in fat, but sacrificial food of lesser sanctity, or, if he was a priest, sacrificial food of the most sacred order, he could eat.

messages.text: Therefore, in the case in the mishna of a ritually impure person who ate leftover forbidden fat from an offering, one who was initially pure was prohibited from eating the food only due to the prohibition of forbidden fat. Once the person became impure, since he became prohibited from eating even pure pieces of sacrificial meat, an additional prohibition is also added to the forbidden fat. The prohibition against an impure person eating sacrificial meat is considered an inclusive prohibition, and therefore it takes effect even though the prohibition against eating forbidden fat already applied.

notes.he: איתסר נמי בחלב משום טומאה והיינו כולל דלא איתוסף איסורא אחפצא אלא אגברא איתוסף איסורא לגבי אחריני כייל נמי להאי באיסורא:
notes.en: Since he became prohibited in [pure] pieces [the word “pure” is printed in parentheses]: he became prohibited also with regard to the fat, because of impurity. This is an inclusive prohibition: the prohibition was not added to the object but to the man. Since a prohibition was added for him with regard to other things, it includes this too in the prohibition.

notes.dh: הוה ליה טמא מיגו דנאסר בחתיכות טהורות
notes.he: דקדשים שהיו מותרין לו קודם (דאינו) [דהיינו] כולל [דנאסר לו] דברים המותרים קודם איתוסף נמי עילוי חלב דהיינו איסור טומאה [על] איסור חלב:
notes.en: He became impure; since he became forbidden in pure pieces: sacrificial food that was permitted to him before. This is inclusive, [since he became forbidden] in things permitted before; it was added also on the fat, that is, the prohibition of impurity [on] the prohibition of fat.

messages.text: And likewise, the forbidden fat was initially forbidden only in consumption. When he consecrated the animal, it became prohibited to derive benefit from it in any manner. Therefore, since the prohibition against deriving any form of benefit was added to it, it was also added with regard to eating the forbidden fat. Consequently, the prohibition against misusing consecrated property, which is an expanded prohibition, applies even to one who eats the forbidden fat.

notes.he: היינו מוסיף דאיתוסף איסורא אחפצא:
notes.en: The prohibition of benefit: this is an expanded prohibition, since a prohibition was added to the object.

notes.dh: אקדשיה לחלב מיגו דאיתוסף ביה איסור הנאה
notes.he: דחלב קדשים אסור בהנאה לכולי עלמא והיינו איסור מוסיף דמוסיף איסור אחרים על איסורו איתוסף נמי איסור לגבי חלב משום הכי חייל נמי איסור מוקדשים על איסור חלב וטמא:
notes.en: He consecrated the fat; since the prohibition of benefit was added to it: for consecrated fat is forbidden for benefit to everyone. This is an expanded prohibition, since it adds others’ prohibition onto his prohibition; a prohibition was added also with regard to the fat. Therefore the prohibition of consecrated items also takes effect on the prohibition of fat and of impurity.

messages.text: And still, the consecrated forbidden fat is prohibited only to an ordinary person, but it is permitted to the Most High, i.e., the altar. When it becomes leftover, since a prohibition was added with regard to the Most High, as it is now prohibited to sacrifice it upon the altar, the expanded prohibition of leftover sacrificial meat is added with regard to an ordinary person as well.

notes.he: נמי איסור מוסיף:
notes.en: Notar: this too is an expanded prohibition.

notes.he: באכילה ובהנאה אבל לגבוה שרי להקטרה:
notes.en: And still, it is forbidden to an ordinary person: in eating and in benefit; but for the Most High it is permitted, for burning.

notes.he: הוי ליה איסור מוסיף דניתוסף [איסור] אחר על איסורו איתוסף נמי איסור נותר עליו על איסור חלב:
notes.en: It became notar: it is an expanded prohibition, since another [prohibition] was added onto its prohibition; the prohibition of notar was added onto it, onto the prohibition of fat.

messages.text: If Yom Kippur, during which the person is prohibited from eating anything, takes effect with regard to it, since a prohibition was added with regard to eating non-sacred food, a prohibition is also added with regard to food that had been consecrated to the Most High. The prohibition against eating on Yom Kippur is an inclusive prohibition, and therefore it takes effect even with regard to eating leftover sacrificial meat.

notes.he: איסור כולל דאיתוסף איסורא אגברא אמידי דמשתרי ליה עד השתא:
notes.en: Yom Kippur: an inclusive prohibition, since a prohibition was added to the man with regard to something that had been permitted to him until now.

notes.he: חל עליה יוה"כ מיגו דאיתסר הוא גבי חולין היינו איסור כולל איתוסף נמי איסור יוה"כ על איסור חלב:
notes.en: Yom Kippur took effect on it; since he became forbidden with regard to non-sacred food: this is an inclusive prohibition; the prohibition of Yom Kippur was added also onto the prohibition of fat.

messages.text: And let the mishna teach: There is a case where one can perform a single act of eating an olive-bulk of food and be liable to bring five sin offerings, rather than four, and interpret it as a case where he ate an olive-bulk from an offering that was sacrificed with the intent to consume it after its appointed time [piggul].

notes.dh: וניתני נמי חייב חמש חטאות ונוקמה
notes.he: חייב חטאת חמישית וכגון דאכל כזית פיגול מאידך בהמה:
notes.en: And let it also teach: liable to five sin offerings, and establish it: liable to a fifth sin offering, for example where he ate an olive-bulk of piggul from another animal.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case of one animal, but is not referring to a case of two animals, and you do not find a case where the prohibitions of leftover sacrificial meat [notar] and piggul apply to one animal. From the moment an offering is rendered piggul it may not be sacrificed or eaten, and therefore it is not subject to the prohibition of notar.

notes.dh: בשתי בהמות לא מיירי ונותר ופיגול בחדא בהמה ליכא
notes.he: דפיגול אינו אלא בד' עבודות של דם הילכך מדפגלה לא חזיא לא לאכילת אדם ולא לאכילת מזבח הלכך לא חייל עליה נותר:
notes.en: It does not speak of two animals, and notar and piggul are not found in one animal: since piggul arises only through the four rites of the blood. Therefore, once he rendered it piggul, it is fit neither for human eating nor for the altar’s eating, and so notar does not take effect on it.

notes.he: משמע דאי חל נותר אפיגול ה"ל למתני ה' חטאות ותימה הלא לא משכחת ה' דהאוכל קדשים בטומאת הגוף לא מחייב אפיגול לפי שאין ניתר לטהורים ולא היה לו שעת הכושר והל"ל נותר ופיגול וטומאה בחד בהמה לא משכחת לה:
notes.en: And notar and piggul are not found in one animal: this implies that if notar took effect on piggul, it would have had to teach five sin offerings. And this is puzzling: one could not find five, since one who eats sacrificial food while his body is impure is not liable for piggul, because it is not permitted to the pure and it never had a time of fitness. It should have said: notar, piggul and impurity are not found in one animal.

notes.he: בחדא בהמה קא מיירי מתני' ונותר ופיגול בחדא בהמה לא משכחת לה דפיגול לא הוי אלא בד' עבודות וכיון שחישב עליה בשעת עבודה לפגלה (ולא) ונתפגלה כולה מיד וליתא באכילה ולא אתי לנותר:
notes.en: The mishna speaks of one animal, and notar and piggul are not found in one animal: since piggul arises only in the four rites, and once he had intent concerning it at the time of the rite to render it piggul, all of it became piggul at once and is not fit for eating, and it does not come to be notar.

messages.text: Why is it not possible for the prohibitions of notar and piggul to apply to the same animal? You find it in a case where one brought upon the altar a limb from an offering that was piggul, as from that time its piggul status has been abrogated, and it becomes notar once the time that it may be sacrificed has passed.

notes.he: דקדשהו מזבח בעבודה. טעמיה דעולא מפרש בזבחים (דף מג.):
notes.en: Its piggul status was abrogated: since the altar sanctified it through the rite. Ulla’s reason is explained in Zevaḥim (43a).

notes.he: בתמיהא:
notes.en: Why not? Asked in astonishment.

notes.he: בחדא בהמה וכגון שהעלה אבר פיגול לגבי מזבח דכיון דהעלה ומשלה בו האור פקע פיגולו ממנו ואם סילקו ושיירו הוה ליה נותר וכי אכלו להאי אבר שפקע פיגולו ונעשה נותר ואכל כזית פיגול משאר איברי פיגול של אותה בהמה ליחייב נמי משום פיגול והוויין תרוויהו בחדא בהמה:
notes.en: You find it in one animal, for example where he brought a piggul limb up to the altar: since he brought it up and the fire took hold of it, its piggul status was abrogated, and if he removed it and left it over, it is notar. And when he ate this limb whose piggul status was abrogated and which became notar, and ate an olive-bulk of piggul from the other piggul limbs of that same animal, let him be liable also for piggul, and both would be in one animal.

messages.text: In the case of a handful of a meal offering that is piggul that one brought upon the altar, its piggul status has been abrogated and it becomes leftover.

notes.he: ואם תאמר אמאי לא פריך מאבר גופיה דאמר פרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים פד. ופה:) דחשיב שחטו חוץ לזמנו כו' אם עלו לא ירדו כך אם ירדו לא יעלו וקאמר עולא ל"ש אלא שלא משלה בו האור אבל משלה בו האור אפילו ירדו יעלו וא"כ ש"מ דעושה לחמו של מזבח ופקע פיגולו ממנו וי"ל דמכל מקום לא תנא ליה בהדיא כל כך דפקע פיגולו ממנו כמו בהדיא דקומץ:
notes.en: Ulla said: a handful of piggul, and so on: And if you ask: why does it not challenge from a limb itself? For it says in the chapter HaMizbe’aḥ Mekadesh (Zevaḥim 84a and 85b) that [an offering] one slaughtered [with intent to eat it] beyond its time, and so on: if they went up they do not come down; so too, if they came down they do not go up. And Ulla said: they taught this only where the fire has not taken hold of it, but where the fire has taken hold of it, even if they came down they go up. If so, we learn that it becomes the altar’s food and its piggul status is abrogated. One may say: in any case it is not taught there as explicitly that its piggul status is abrogated as it is explicitly taught with the handful.

notes.he: במנחות הקשה רש"י פרק הקומץ (דף יד.) אמאי איצטריך קרא למעט קומץ מפיגול תיפוק לי דלא קרב המתיר כמצותו ותירץ דמיירי במשלה בו האור ברובו שהותרו השירים כדאמרינן קומץ מאימתי מתיר השיריים באכילה משהוצת האור ברובו וקשה דא"כ (לוקים) דפקע פיגולו ממנו כדמוכח הכא ויש לומר דמיירי שחציו העלה ע"ג המזבח וחציו לא העלה דלא פקע פיגולו מן החצי שנשאר ואם תאמר ואפי' לכתחלה נמי מעלין ליה כדאמרינן פרק בית שמאי (זבחים מג:) האי קומץ דפלגיה אנחיה אארעא אסיקנא ליה לכתחלה וי"ל שאני התם שהיה כולו מתחלה ע"ג המזבח ואח"כ הוריד חציו למטה אבל הכא לא היה על המזבח וא"ת מנחת נסכים ומנחת כהן משיח שהם כולן כליל אמאי צריך קרא למעט אותם מפיגול והלא אינה מתרת שום דבר ויש לומר כיון שקדשו בכלי הוי כמו קרבו מתירין וקבעה בפיגול ולכך צריך קרא למעט:
notes.en: Its piggul status is abrogated: In Menaḥot, in the chapter HaKometz (14a), Rashi asked why a verse is needed to exclude the handful from piggul; let me derive it from the fact that what permits it was not offered as commanded. He answered that it speaks where the fire took hold of most of it, so that the remainder was permitted, as we say: from when does the handful permit the remainder to be eaten? From when the fire has caught in most of it. But this is difficult: if so, its piggul status would be abrogated, as is evident here. One may say that it speaks where he brought half of it up onto the altar and half he did not, and its piggul status is not abrogated from the half that remained. And if you ask: even initially one brings it up, as we say in the chapter Beit Shammai (Zevaḥim 43b): a handful half of which he set on the ground, we bring it up even initially. One may say: there it is different, since all of it was on the altar at first and afterward he brought half of it down, but here it was not on the altar. And if you ask: the meal offering of libations and the meal offering of the anointed priest, which are burned whole, why is a verse needed to exclude them from piggul, when they permit nothing? One may say: since they were sanctified in the vessel, it is as if what permits them was offered, and it fixed them in piggul; therefore a verse is needed to exclude them.

notes.he: ומנלן דפקע פיגול בהכי כדאמר עולא במס' זבחים קומץ שהוא פיגול והעלהו לגבי מזבח כיון שמשלה בו האור להורידו ושיירו ופקע פיגול ונעשה נותר אפי' הכי באבר אחד קא מיירי מתניתין דחייב עליו ונותר ופיגול בחדא בהמה ובחד אבר לא משכחת לה:
notes.en: And from where do we know that piggul status is abrogated in this way? As Ulla said in tractate Zevaḥim: a handful that is piggul that one brought up to the altar, once the fire has taken hold of it, [if] he took it down and left it over, its piggul status is abrogated and it becomes notar. Even so, the mishna speaks of one limb, for which he is liable, and notar and piggul are not found in one animal and in one limb.

messages.text: Consequently, he is liable with regard to the limb that was offered for violating the prohibition of notar, and is liable with regard to the rest of the animal for violating the prohibition of piggul.
The mishna is referring to one limb, but it is not referring to two limbs, and you do not find notar and piggul with regard to one limb.

Why is there no such case? You find it in a situation where one brought a limb from a piggul offering upon the altar, and he placed half of it upon the altar and half of it outside of the altar. In such a case, with regard to that portion of the limb which he placed upon the altar, its piggul status has been abrogated and it becomes notar.
In the case of a handful of a meal offering that is piggul that one brought upon the altar, its piggul status has been abrogated and it becomes notar.
By contrast, the part of the limb that was not placed upon the altar retains its status as piggul.

No, the status of piggul cannot be abrogated from part of a limb. Rather, if the majority of the limb is on the altar, then throw it on the altar, i.e., the entire limb has the status of being on the altar. If the majority of the limb is outside the altar, throw it outside, i.e., it is considered as though the limb was not placed on the altar at all.
messages.lead: The Sage answering the question said to the questioner:
messages.quote: he placed half of it upon the altar and half of it outside of the altar

notes.he: לכולו אבר אמזבח והוי כוליה נותר כו':
notes.en: If the majority is on the altar, throw it on the altar: the whole limb [counts as] on the altar, and all of it is notar, and so on.

notes.he: בחד אבר כגון שהעלה עליה אבר פיגול לגבי מזבח דפלגיה דאבר אנחיה אמזבח ופלגיה דאבר הוה תלוי אבראי דמזבח ואיכא בחד אבר נותר ופיגול לא איפשר למיהוי בחד אבר דלא אפשר לצמצם לאנחיה מפלגיה דאברו במקום דאיכא רובה דאבר תמן שדינן ליה כיון דאזלת בתר רובה:
notes.en: Why are they not found in one limb? For example, where he brought a piggul limb up to the altar and placed half the limb on the altar while half the limb hung outside the altar; then in one limb there would be notar and piggul. [The answer:] It is impossible for there to be [both] in one limb, since one cannot be so exact as to place precisely half of the limb; where the majority of the limb is, there we cast it, since you go after the majority.

messages.text: If so, one can resolve the dilemma that Rami bar Ḥama raised: Does one follow the majority with regard to limbs or not? According to the previous interpretation of the mishna, one does follow the majority with regard to limbs.

notes.he: האי בעיא בפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין ע.):
notes.en: Does one follow the majority with regard to limbs, and so on: this dilemma is in the chapter Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 70a).

notes.dh: תפשוט דבעי רמי בר חמא הלכו באיברים אחר הרוב
notes.he: פירש בקונטרס היינו בעיא דפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין ע.) ואינו נראה לר"ת דמאי שייכא ההיא בעיא להך דהכא דהתם מיירי אם יצא חציו ברוב אבר אי הוי כילוד או לא לכך נראה לפרש דהיינו בעיא דפרק מזבח מקדש (זבחים פז.) דאיבעיא להו אויר מזבח כמזבח או לא כו' רובו לכבש ככבש דמי רובו למזבח כמזבח דמי תפשוט דבעי רמי בר חמא יש חיבור בעולין או לא:
notes.en: Resolve the dilemma that Rami bar Ḥama raised: does one follow the majority with regard to limbs: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that this is the dilemma in the chapter Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 70a). This does not seem right to Rabbeinu Tam, for what does that dilemma have to do with this one? There it concerns whether, if half came out with the majority of a limb, it counts as born or not. Therefore it seems one should explain that it is the dilemma in the chapter Mizbe’aḥ Mekadesh (Zevaḥim 87a), where they asked whether the airspace of the altar is like the altar or not, and so on: if most of it is over the ramp it is like the ramp; if most of it is over the altar it is like the altar. Resolve the dilemma of Rami bar Ḥama: whether there is joining with regard to burnt offerings or not.

notes.he: בבהמה המקשה הלכו באברים אחר הרוב אי לא. אלא מדלא איפשט ליה מהכא ש"מ דלא אזלינן בתר רוב אבר. ולוקמה בחד אבר כדאמרן וליחייב נמי משום פיגול:
notes.en: Resolve the dilemma that Rami bar Ḥama raised in [the chapter] Behema HaMaksha: does one follow the majority with regard to limbs or not? Rather, since it was not resolved for him from here, learn from this that we do not follow the majority of a limb; so let it be established in one limb as we said, and let him be liable also for piggul.

messages.text: Rather, the reason that the mishna did not mention the prohibition of piggul is that it is referring to the consumption of one olive-bulk of forbidden fat, and is not referring to two olive-bulks. Even if parts of one limb can have the status of piggul and other parts can be leftover sacrificial meat, one single olive-bulk cannot have both statuses.

notes.he: חלב דאיסור קמיירי בשני זיתי חלב לא קמיירי:
notes.en: One olive-bulk: it speaks of [one olive-bulk of] forbidden fat; it does not speak of two olive-bulks of fat.

notes.he: תנא דמתניתין וכזית אחד לא משכחת פיגול ונותר דאי אנחיה לפלגיה דזית אמזבח ופלגא אבראי אין הקטרה לפחות מכזית ולא קא פקע פיגול מיניה והוי פיגול אלא לא משכחת לה פיגול ונותר בחד אבר אלא באבר שיש בו שני זיתי חלב ובב' זיתים לא קא מיירי תנא:
notes.en: Rather, the tanna of the mishna speaks of one olive-bulk, and in one olive-bulk you do not find piggul and notar: for if he placed half the olive-bulk on the altar and half outside, there is no burning of less than an olive-bulk, so its piggul status is not abrogated and it remains piggul. So you find piggul and notar in one limb only in a limb that has two olive-bulks of fat, and the tanna does not speak of two olive-bulks.

messages.text: And is the mishna not referring to a case of more than one olive-bulk? But isn’t it taught that one is liable to bring a sin offering for eating on Yom Kippur, and on Yom Kippur it is only eating the volume of a large date that obligates one to bring a sin offering, and the volume of a large date contains the volume of two olives?

notes.he: דכך בית הבליעה מחזיק:
notes.en: A date-bulk contains two olive-bulks: since that is what the throat holds.

messages.text: It is referring to a case where he eats a kidney with the fat attached to it. He is liable to bring three of the sin offerings enumerated in the mishna for eating the olive-bulk of fat, and the additional amount of kidney he eats brings his total consumption to the volume of a large date, so that he is liable for eating on Yom Kippur.
messages.quote: the volume of a large date contains the volume of two olives

notes.he: דאאכילת חלב מחייב שלש חטאות ואשם וגורם נמי להשלמת אכילת כותבת וזית של כוליא משלים לכותבת הילכך לא תנא פגול דבשני זיתי חלב לא קמיירי. ואי תימא לוקים כגון שהעלה זית של כוליא אמזבח דהוה חלב פיגול ולכוליא נותר א"כ לא מהני נותר אזית דחלב ואנן בעינן דליהוי חד אכולהו דאכילה קתני דהיינו כזית:
notes.en: For example, where he ate a kidney with its fat: for eating the fat he is liable to three sin offerings and a guilt offering, and it also counts toward completing the eating of a date-bulk, while the olive-bulk of kidney completes the date-bulk. Therefore it does not teach piggul, since it does not speak of two olive-bulks of fat. And if you say: let it be established where he brought the olive-bulk of kidney up onto the altar, so that the fat is piggul and the kidney notar; if so, the notar does not apply to the olive-bulk of fat, and we need them all to apply to one [olive-bulk], since it teaches “eating,” that is, an olive-bulk.

notes.he: (גליו"ן) אלא בכזית אחד מיירי ואי אנחיה לפלגיה דזית אמזבח אין הקטרה בפחות מכזית:
notes.en: [A marginal gloss:] Rather, it speaks of one olive-bulk; and if he placed half the olive-bulk on the altar, there is no burning of less than an olive-bulk.

notes.he: ואם נפשך לומר ליחייב אכוליא משום פיגול ואחלבה משום נותר לא מצי למימר הכי דטמא שאכל קתני דבחלב עצמו בעי לאוקומי לכולהו איסורי. פירוש מורי:
notes.en: For example, where he ate a kidney with its fat: and if you should wish to say, let him be liable for the kidney on account of piggul and for its fat on account of notar, one cannot say so, since it teaches “an impure person who ate” [forbidden fat]; it wants to establish all the prohibitions in the fat itself. This is my teacher’s explanation.

notes.he: תימה מ"ש מב' זיתי חלב מיהו השתא ליכא למימר דחלק החלב מעל הכוליא ויניח הכוליא ע"ג המזבח ויחול עליו נותר דבב' אברים כלומר בב' חתיכות לא מיירי:
notes.en: For example, where he ate a kidney with its fat: this is puzzling: how is this different from two olive-bulks of fat? Nevertheless, now one cannot say that he separated the fat from the kidney and placed the kidney on the altar so that notar would take effect on it, since it does not speak of two limbs, that is, two pieces.

notes.dh: ולא הא קתני יוה"כ כו' אמר ר' זירא
notes.he: הכי משכחת לה דלענין יוה"כ הוי שיעור שלם ולא משכחת ביה פיגול ונותר כגון דאכל כוליא בחלבה שהכוליא כזית וחלבה כזית והיינו חד אבר ובחלבה דכזית הוא לא מצית לאוקומיה פיגול ונותר כדאמרן לעיל דאין היקש לפחות מכזית ואם נפשך לומר ליחייב אכוליא משום פיגול ואחלבה משום נותר לא מצית למימר הכי דטמא שאכל חלב והוא נותר דמן המוקדשין קתני אלמא דבחלב עצמו בעי לאוקמי לכולהו איסורי ופיגול ונותר לא משכחת ביה בחד זית וכזית דכוליא לא אתי אלא לאשלומי כותבת ולא מצי למימר דהוי פיגול כדאמרן:
notes.en: And does it not? But it teaches Yom Kippur, and so on. Rabbi Zeira said: this is how you find it, that with regard to Yom Kippur it is a full measure and yet you do not find piggul and notar in it: for example, where he ate a kidney with its fat, the kidney being an olive-bulk and its fat an olive-bulk, and this is one limb. And in its fat, which is an olive-bulk, you cannot establish piggul and notar, as we said above, since there is no heikesh [so the printed text; above he said “no burning”] of less than an olive-bulk. And if you should wish to say, let him be liable for the kidney on account of piggul and for its fat on account of notar, you cannot say so, since it teaches “an impure person who ate fat” that is notar from consecrated items; evidently it wants to establish all the prohibitions in the fat itself, and piggul and notar are not found in one olive-bulk. And the olive-bulk of kidney comes only to complete the date-bulk, and one cannot say it is piggul, as we said.

messages.text: It is referring to a case where he ate an olive-bulk of the fat and completed the volume of a large date with dates.
messages.quote: the volume of a large date contains the volume of two olives

notes.he: להכי לא תנא פיגול דלא מיירי בשני זיתי חלב ודקא קשיא לך כותבת כגון דמלייה לחלב בתמרי והשלימו לככותבת:
notes.en: Rav Pappa said: the reason it does not teach piggul is that it does not speak of two olive-bulks of fat. And as for what troubled you about the date-bulk: for example, where he filled out the fat with dates and completed it to a date-bulk.

notes.he: הכא במאי עסקינן דחייב ד' חטאות בלבד כגון דלא הוה אלא כזית חלב ואכל עמו תמרי עד דמלייה לכותבת ולא מצי לאוקומיה ביה פיגול:
notes.en: Rav Pappa said: With what are we dealing here, where he is liable to four sin offerings only? For example, where there was only an olive-bulk of fat, and he ate dates with it until he filled it out to a date-bulk, and one cannot establish piggul in it.

messages.text: Rav Adda bar Aḥa teaches that the mishna is stating that one can be liable to bring five sin offerings for one act of eating, not just four, and he interprets it to be referring to a case where one ate an olive-bulk of piggul from another animal together with the olive-bulk of forbidden fat, and he does not answer in accordance with these answers that we answered in the name of Rav Pappa and Rabbi Zeira.
messages.quote: five sin offerings, rather than four

notes.dh: ומתרץ לה כגון דאכל כזית פיגול
notes.he: מבהמה אחרת בהדה:
notes.en: And he resolves it as where he ate an olive-bulk of piggul: from another animal, together with it.

notes.dh: רב אחא בר יעקב כו' ומתרץ לה כגון דאכל
notes.he: נמי בהדיה דהאי כזית חלב כזית פיגול מבהמה אחריתי ולא משני כהני שינויי דקא משנינן דבחדא בהמה ובחדא אבר ובחדא זית מיירי אלא קא סבר אפי' בב' בהמות מיירי ובב' זיתים:
notes.en: Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov, and so on [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf reads Rav Adda bar Aḥa]. And he resolves it as where he ate, together with this olive-bulk of fat, an olive-bulk of piggul from another animal; and he does not answer with these answers that we answer, that it speaks of one animal, one limb and one olive-bulk. Rather, he holds that it speaks even of two animals and two olive-bulks.

messages.text: And let the mishna teach that one can be liable to bring six sin offerings, and interpret it as referring to a case where he consumed an olive-bulk of blood in addition to the other two olive-bulks.

notes.he: חייב שש חטאות ונוקמה נמי כגון דאכל כזית שלישי מדם:
notes.en: If so, let it teach: liable to six sin offerings, and establish it also where he ate a third olive-bulk, of blood.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to one act of eating, but is not referring to two acts of eating, and the Sages calculated that one’s throat does not hold more than two olive-bulks at once.

notes.dh: אין בית הבליעה מחזיק יותר מב' זיתים
notes.he: פירוש כדרך אכילה:
notes.en: The throat does not hold more than two olive-bulks: that is, in the normal manner of eating.

notes.dh: בחדא אכילה מיירי שיכול לבלוע ביחד ושיערו חכמים כו'
notes.he: הילכך לא תנא דם:
notes.en: It speaks of one eating, that he can swallow together, and the Sages calculated, and so on. Therefore it does not teach blood.

messages.caption: Why the mishna counts four sin offerings and not five or six: each proposal, and the narrowing the Gemara gives in answer.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Meir says: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out from the private domain into the public domain while eating it, he would be liable to bring a sin offering for performing a prohibited labor on Shabbat.

And let the mishna teach: If he carried it out he is liable, as the mishna is referring to one who ate on Yom Kippur, which is also a day when labor is prohibited. What is the reason that it teaches: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out he is liable? Why mention Shabbat at all?

notes.he: דהא יה"כ הוא:
notes.en: And let it teach: if he carried it out he is liable: since it is Yom Kippur.

notes.he: ביוה"כ חייב מ"ט תני אם היה שבת והוציאו:
notes.en: And let it also teach: if he carried it out on Yom Kippur he is liable. What is the reason it teaches: if it was Shabbat and he carried it out?

messages.text: That is to say that the joining of courtyards in order to permit carrying, and the general prohibition against carrying from one domain to another, apply with regard to Shabbat, but the joining of courtyards and the prohibition against carrying do not apply with regard to Yom Kippur.

notes.he: פירוש נתערבה הוצאה עם שאר מלאכות לשבת ולא נתערבה הוצאה עם שאר מלאכות בי"ה. לשון מורי ז"ל:
notes.en: Joining and carrying for Shabbat: that is, carrying was joined with the other labors for Shabbat, and carrying was not joined with the other labors for Yom Kippur. These are my teacher’s words, of blessed memory.

notes.dh: אמר רפרם זאת אומרת עירוב והוצאה לשבת
notes.he: כלומר לשבת יש בו איסור לטלטל בחצירות בלא עירוב ויש בו איסור הוצאה מרה"י לרה"ר ואין עירוב והוצאה ליוה"כ. מדלא קתני ואם הוציאו ביוה"כ:
notes.en: Rafram said: That is to say, joining and carrying for Shabbat: that is, for Shabbat there is a prohibition to carry in courtyards without a joining [eruv], and there is a prohibition of carrying out from the private domain to the public domain; and there is no joining and carrying for Yom Kippur. [This follows] from the fact that it does not teach: and if he carried it out on Yom Kippur.

messages.text: From where is this conclusion derived? Perhaps the joining of courtyards and the prohibition against carrying do apply to Yom Kippur, and this is what the mishna is teaching: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out from one domain to another he is liable due to the prohibition against carrying on Shabbat and also due to the prohibition against carrying on Yom Kippur.
messages.quote: the joining of courtyards and the prohibition against carrying do not apply with regard to Yom Kippur

notes.he: וא"ת מה שייך זה לענין אכילה ויש לומר דהכי פירושו והוציאו בפיו דכיון שהניחו בפיו ברה"י והוציאה ברשות הרבים מחייב משום הוצאה דבליעתו היא הנחתו דהא מוציא שתי אותיות וכתבן כשהוא מהלך חייב דכתיבתן זו היא הנחתן:
notes.en: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out: And if you ask: what does this have to do with eating? One may say that this is its meaning: he carried it out in his mouth. Since he placed it in his mouth in the private domain and carried it out into the public domain, he is liable for carrying, since his swallowing is its placing down; for one who carries out and writes two letters while walking is liable, since their writing is their placing down.

messages.text: Rather, if the statement of Rafram was stated, it was stated with regard to this case, as it is taught in a baraita:

The verse states with regard to the scapegoat of Yom Kippur: “And he shall send it away with an appointed man into the wilderness” (Leviticus 16:21). The word “man” is mentioned in order to render a non-priest fit for this task. The term “appointed” indicates that the scapegoat is always sent away at the appropriate time, even when the appointed man is in a state of ritual impurity, and even when Yom Kippur occurs on Shabbat. In addition, the word “appointed” is referring to one who was designated for the task the day before.

verse.he: וְסָמַךְ אַהֲרֹן אֶת־שְׁתֵּי יָדָו עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׂעִיר הַחַי וְהִתְוַדָּה עָלָיו אֶת־כׇּל־עֲוֺנֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶת־כׇּל־פִּשְׁעֵיהֶם לְכׇל־חַטֹּאתָם וְנָתַן אֹתָם עַל־רֹאשׁ הַשָּׂעִיר וְשִׁלַּח בְּיַד־אִישׁ עִתִּי הַמִּדְבָּרָה׃
verse.en: Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities and transgressions of the Israelites, whatever their sins, putting them on the head of the goat; and it shall be sent off to the wilderness through a designated uncertain. agent.

notes.he: שיזמנוהו מאתמול להוליך השעיר:
notes.en: Appointed: one whom they designated the day before to lead away the goat.

notes.he: ואפילו בטומאה ואפי' אם הוא טמא המוליכו מדקתני ואפי' בשבת דאיצטריך (עירוב) למישרי בשבת ולא יוה"כ זאת אומרת עירוב כו':
notes.en: Appointed: one who is accustomed to lead it into the wilderness. And even in impurity: even if the one leading it is impure. From the fact that it teaches “and even on Shabbat,” it was necessary to permit it on Shabbat and not on Yom Kippur: that is to say, joining, and so on.

messages.text: The baraita taught that the word “appointed” indicates that the scapegoat is sent away even on Shabbat.

That is to say that the joining of courtyards and the prohibition against carrying apply with regard to Shabbat, but the joining of courtyards and the prohibition against carrying do not apply with regard to Yom Kippur.

notes.he: מדקתני אפילו בשבת אין עירוב והוצאה ליה"כ דאם יש איסור הוצאה ליה"כ אמאי איצטריך לרבויי שבת הא דחי יה"כ והוא הדין לשבת:
notes.en: That is to say: since it teaches “even on Shabbat,” there is no joining and carrying for Yom Kippur. For if there were a prohibition of carrying on Yom Kippur, why was it necessary to include Shabbat? It overrides Yom Kippur, and the same would apply to Shabbat.

messages.text: From where does he cite proof for this inference? The case of the scapegoat is different, as its validity on Yom Kippur is in this manner. Even if the prohibition against carrying does apply on Yom Kippur, the Torah explicitly commanded that the scapegoat be sent away on that day, and therefore it is permitted.
messages.quote: That is to say that the joining of courtyards and the prohibition against carrying apply with regard to Shabbat

notes.he: מיה"כ לא שמעינן לשבת דיה"כ שאני דהכשר מצותו בכך דומיא דתמידין שקריבין בשבת:
notes.en: Perhaps: from Yom Kippur we would not learn about Shabbat, since Yom Kippur is different, as the fulfillment of its mitzva is in this, like the daily offerings that are sacrificed on Shabbat.

messages.text: Rather, the statement cited in the name of Rafram is an error [beruta], and it was not actually stated in the study hall.

notes.he: ובפרק שני שעירים (יומא סו:) איתא נמי הא דהכא ולא דחי דילמא שאני שעיר המשתלח כו' כדדחי הכא אלא רגילות הוא דברי תורה עניים במקומם ועשירים במקום אחר:
notes.en: Rather, Rafram’s is an error: In the chapter Shnei Se’irim (Yoma 66b) this passage also appears, and it does not reject it with “perhaps the scapegoat is different” as it rejects it here. Rather, it is common that words of Torah are poor in their place and rich in another place.

notes.he: ממאי אימא לך דיש עירוב והוצאה נמי ליוה"כ לכל שאר מילי ושאני שעיר המשתלח (דאמאי) [דמשו"ה] לית ביה איסור עירוב דהכשירו מצותו ביוה"כ בכך להוליכו למדבר אלא דרפרם ברותא היא:
notes.en: From where [is this proven]? I can tell you that there is joining and carrying for Yom Kippur too, for all other matters, and the scapegoat is different, [and for that reason] there is no prohibition of joining for it, since the fulfillment of its mitzva on Yom Kippur is in this, to lead it to the wilderness. Rather, Rafram’s is an error.

messages.text: Mishna

There is a case where one can engage in a single act of intercourse and be liable to bring six sin offerings for it. How so? It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his daughter to be liable due to having violated the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his daughter, his sister, the wife of his brother, the wife of his father’s brother, a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

notes.he: שבא על אמו והולידה:
notes.en: Mishna. His daughter and his sister: where he had intercourse with his mother and fathered her.

notes.he: שנשאת לו קודם לכן ולאחר מיתתו נשאה אחי אביו ובא זה אביה עליה בנדתה:
notes.en: And the wife of his brother: where she married him [his brother] beforehand, and after his death his father’s brother married her, and this man, her father, had intercourse with her while she was menstruating.

notes.dh: יש בא ביאה אחת כו' הבא על בתו חייב עליה משום בתו ואחותו
notes.he: היינו כגון שבא על אמו והולידה בת (ממנה) [ממנו] ונשאה אחיו מאביו ומת אחיו שנשאה ונשאה אחי אביו דודו ומת ואח"כ נישאת לאיש אחר והיא נדה ובא עליה אביה חייב שש חטאות משום בתו ואחותו ואשת אחיו כו':
notes.en: There is one who engages in one act of intercourse, and so on; one who has intercourse with his daughter is liable for her on account of his daughter and his sister. That is, for example, where he had intercourse with his mother and fathered a daughter from her; and his brother from his father married her, and the brother who married her died; and his father’s brother, his uncle, married her and died; and afterward she married another man, and she is menstruating, and her father had intercourse with her. He is liable to six sin offerings: on account of his daughter, his sister, the wife of his brother, and so on.

messages.text: Gemara
How could one become liable to bring multiple sin offerings? But Rabbi Meir does not hold that a prohibition takes effect where another prohibition already exists.
messages.quote: liable to bring six sin offerings for it

notes.dh: והא לית ליה לר' מאיר כו'
notes.he: דהא לא בעי' לאוקומי לעיל אלא באיסור כולל ומוסיף:
notes.en: But Rabbi Meir does not hold, and so on: for above we wanted to establish it only with an inclusive and an expanded prohibition.

messages.text: Although he generally does not hold that a prohibition takes effect where another prohibition already exists, with regard to an expanded prohibition and a more inclusive prohibition, he does hold that it takes effect where another prohibition already exists.

Consequently, the ruling stated in the mishna applies in a case where one engaged in intercourse with his mother and thereby fathered a daughter, so that the prohibitions against engaging in intercourse with his daughter and with his sister come into effect simultaneously. If that daughter married his brother, then since a prohibition was added with regard to his other brothers, to whom she has now become forbidden, it is an expanded prohibition, and therefore a further prohibition is added with regard to him as well.

notes.dh: מיגו דאיתוסף איסורא בה לגבי שאר אחין
notes.he: משום אשת אח איתוסף נמי איסורא גבי דידיה:
notes.en: Since a prohibition was added to her with regard to the other brothers: on account of a brother’s wife, a prohibition was added with regard to him too.

notes.he: פירוש משום אשת אח וא"ת והא ממזרת היא ואם כן היאך אסורה לאחיו משום אשת אח איך חל איסור אשת אח על איסור ממזרת ויש לומר דמיירי דאחיו נמי ממזר ואם כן ליכא איסור ממזרת דהוא עצמו כמו כן ממזר ועי"ל דאיסור חמור חל שפיר על איסור קל כדפרישית לעיל:
notes.en: She married his brother; since a prohibition was added, and so on: that is, on account of a brother’s wife. And if you ask: but she is a mamzeret; if so, how is she forbidden to his brother on account of a brother’s wife? How does the prohibition of a brother’s wife take effect on the prohibition of a mamzeret? One may say that it speaks where his brother too is a mamzer, and so there is no prohibition of a mamzeret, since he himself is likewise a mamzer. And one may further say that a severe prohibition does take effect on a lighter prohibition, as I explained above.

notes.he: דכי בא על בתו איסור בתו ואחותו באין כאחד ניסת לאחיו מיגו דאיתוסף איסורא לגבי אחין כולן בשאינה זקוקה לייבום איתוסף נמי לגבי דידיה (דאבוה) [משום אחוה] והיינו איסור מוסיף שניתוספו אחרים על איסורו שאיסורה נמי לאחין כולן. נישאת לאחי אביו היינו נמי איסור מוסיף שנאסרה נמי על אחי אביו. ואשת איש ונדה היינו נמי איסור מוסיף שניתוספו אחרים נמי על איסורו:
notes.en: A simultaneous prohibition: for when he has intercourse with his daughter, the prohibitions of his daughter and his sister come together. She married his brother; since a prohibition was added with regard to all the brothers, where she is not bound to them for levirate marriage, it was added also with regard to him [on account of a brother]. This is an expanded prohibition, where others were added to his prohibition, since her prohibition applies also to all the brothers. She married his father’s brother: this too is an expanded prohibition, since she became forbidden also to his father’s brothers. And a married woman and a menstruating woman: this too is an expanded prohibition, since others too were added to his prohibition.

messages.text: If she later married his father’s brother, then since a prohibition is added with regard to the sons of his father’s other brothers, a prohibition is also added with regard to him.

notes.dh: נשאת לאחי אביו מיגו דאיתוסף איסורא לגבי אחיו איתוסף לגבי דידיה
notes.he: ולגבי אחיו משום אשת אחי האב:
notes.en: She married his father’s brother; since a prohibition was added with regard to his brothers, it was added with regard to him: and with regard to his brothers, [she is forbidden] on account of the wife of the father’s brother. [Rashi’s lemma reads “his brothers”; the Davidson English reads “the sons of his father’s other brothers,” and the Aramaic of the daf “his father’s other brothers.”]

notes.he: ל"א ה"ג מיגו דאיתוסף איסורא לגבי בני אחי אביו משום אשת אב:
notes.en: Another version: we read, “since a prohibition was added with regard to the sons of his father’s brothers,” on account of a father’s wife.

notes.dh: מיגו דאיתוסף איסורא לגבי בני אחים וכו'
notes.he: היינו ב' שמות אשת אב ואשת אחי אביו באיסור מוסיף:
notes.en: Since a prohibition was added with regard to the sons of the brothers, and so on: these are two categories, a father’s wife and the wife of his father’s brother, in an expanded prohibition.

messages.text: If she becomes, or remains, a married woman, since a prohibition is added with regard to every man in the world other than her husband, a prohibition is added with regard to him as well. If she then becomes a menstruating woman, since a prohibition is added with regard to her husband, a prohibition is added with regard to him as well.

messages.caption: The mishna’s six sin offerings for one act, as the Gemara builds them: two prohibitions that come at once, then four that each take effect because they are expanded prohibitions.

messages.text: Mishna

It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his daughter’s daughter to be liable to bring sin offerings due to the unwitting violation of the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his daughter’s daughter, and his daughter-in-law, and the wife of his brother, and the wife of his father’s brother, and his wife’s sister, and a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

notes.he: שנשאה בנו:
notes.en: Mishna. His daughter’s daughter and his daughter-in-law: where his son married her.

notes.he: שהיה נשוי את בת חתנו שהיא אחות בת בתו מן האב כגון שהיתה לו בת מאשה אחרת ונשאה זה האב חמיו של בעל בתו וכשבא זה על בתו של חתנו שהיא לו בת בתו היתה אחות אשתו:
notes.en: And his wife’s sister: where he was married to the daughter of his son-in-law, who is the sister of his daughter’s daughter through the father. For example, where he [the son-in-law] had a daughter from another wife, and this man, the father-in-law of his daughter’s husband, married her; and when this man had intercourse with the daughter of his son-in-law who is his daughter’s daughter, she was his wife’s sister.

notes.he: שמת בנו ונשאה אחיו של זה:
notes.en: And the wife of his brother: where his son died and this man’s brother married her.

notes.he: שמת אחיו ונשאה אחי אביו:
notes.en: And the wife of his father’s brother: where his brother died and his father’s brother married her.

notes.he: הקשה רבינו ברוך אמאי לא חשיב בהדייהו בת בנה כגון שניסת בתו לבן אשתו וילדה לו בת דהויא בת בתו ובת בנה בבת אחת וגם בסיפא קשה אמאי לא תני בת בנה ובת בתה דמשכחת לה ביעקב שנשא רחל ולאה שאינם אחיות ויש לה בן לרחל מאדם אחר ונשא בת לאה שהיתה לה מיעקב וילדה בת לאה בת ובא יעקב עליה הרי היא בת בן אשתו ובת בתו ולפי מה שפי' לקמן דמתני' לא מיירי רק באיסור מוסיף ניחא שפיר והקשה הקדוש ה"ר יום טוב אמאי לא תני חמותו כגון שנשא בת בת בתו דבת בתו היא חמותו וי"ל דת"ק לא מיירי בעבד איסורא ומהאי טעמא לא תני אם חמותו ואם חמיו ושניות הן ואפילו לרבי יוסי נמי דמיירי בעבר זקן ונשאה יש לומר להכי לא תני להו דהוי איסור כולל ואפילו לר' חייא דאמר פרק ד' אחין (יבמות לב: ולג.) לר' יוסי מחייב תרתי משום איסור כולל היינו באיסור כולל בשם אחד אבל בשני שמות לא ומש"ה ניחא לדידיה גבי אשת איש ונעשת חמותו דלא אמרי' נידון בחמותו משום דשני שמות הן:
notes.en: In brief: Rabbeinu Barukh asked why the mishna does not also count “her son’s daughter,” for example where his daughter married his wife’s son and bore him a daughter, who is at once his daughter’s daughter and his wife’s son’s daughter. And in the latter clause, why does it not teach “her son’s daughter and her daughter’s daughter”? This can be found where Jacob married Rachel and Leah, who are not sisters; Rachel had a son from another man, who married Leah’s daughter by Jacob; Leah’s daughter bore a daughter, and Jacob had intercourse with her, so that she is his wife’s son’s daughter and his daughter’s daughter. [Tosafot answer:] according to what is explained below, that the mishna speaks only of an expanded prohibition, this is well. The holy Rabbi Yom Tov asked why it does not teach “his mother-in-law,” for example where he married his daughter’s daughter’s daughter, so that his daughter’s daughter is his mother-in-law. One may say that the first tanna does not speak of one who committed a transgression [in marrying], and for this reason it does not teach his mother-in-law’s mother and his father-in-law’s mother, which are secondary relatives. Even according to Rabbi Yosei, who speaks of the elder who transgressed and married her, one may say it does not teach them because that would be an inclusive prohibition; and even according to Rabbi Ḥiyya, who says (Yevamot 32b–33a) that according to Rabbi Yosei one is liable to two on account of an inclusive prohibition, that is an inclusive prohibition within one category, but not in two categories. For this reason, according to him, it is well with regard to a married woman who became his mother-in-law, that we do not say he is judged on account of his mother-in-law, since they are two categories. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: ואומר הר"י דלא גרס ליה דאם כן שבע הוו ואדתני לעיל שש ליתני שבע ואם תאמר וליתני שבע וליחשוב אחות אשתו וכגון שדינה בת יעקב ניסת לאדם מעלמא וילדה לו בת ואותו אדם היה לו בת אחרת מאשה אחרת ונשאה יעקב ואם כן הרי בת דינה ליעקב בת בתו ואחות אשתו וחיילא איסור אחות אשתו באיסור כולל מיגו דמיתסר בשאר אחיות משום אחות אשה איתסר נמי בבת דינה משום אחות אשה ויש לומר דלא תני רק איסורי דמודי בהו ר' יוסי ומיירי בסיפא דהיינו איסור מוסיף ואפילו לר' חייא דאמר דאית ליה לר' יוסי איסור כולל י"ל לא נחת למיתני במתני' רק איסור מוסיף וא"ת מכל מקום אמאי לא תנא אחות אשתו ובבת אחת וכגון שיעקב נשא אחותו נכרית של בת דינה בת יעקב וילדה לו בת השתא הויא אותו בת של דינה בת בתו של יעקב ואחות אשתו ויש לומר דבאיסורא שחל ע"י קדושין לא תני אלא אותה שחל האיסור מיד בשעת קדושין והשתא מיד שנשא יעקב בת האיש לא היה שום איסור עד שנולדה דינה מאותו האיש אז חל איסור אחות אשתו עם איסור בת בתו וא"ת ובגמרא נמי דקאמר מודי ליה באיסור מוסיף מנליה דילמא כולה מתני' באיסור בת אחת מיירי וכגון שנתקדשה הלה פחות מבת ג' שנים דכי נשלם שנה שלישית אז חלו כל האיסורין וחשיב במתני' בבת אחת וי"ל דלא חשיב איסורא שע"י קדושין אלא כשחלין בשעת קדושין ואי בבת אחת הויין עלה הרי לא חלו שום איסור עד גמר שלש שנים ויום אחד ועוד י"ל דמתני' לא אתיא לאורויי רק באיסור מוסיף כמו שפירשתי:
notes.en: In brief: And his wife’s sister: the Ri says that this is not part of the text, for if so there would be seven, and instead of teaching six above it should teach seven. If you ask: let it teach seven [here] and count his wife’s sister, as where Dinah, Jacob’s daughter, married some man and bore him a daughter, that man had another daughter from another wife, and Jacob married her, so that Dinah’s daughter is Jacob’s daughter’s daughter and his wife’s sister, with the prohibition of a wife’s sister taking effect as an inclusive prohibition: one may say that the mishna teaches only prohibitions that Rabbi Yosei concedes, and the latter clause speaks of an expanded prohibition; and even according to Rabbi Ḥiyya, who says Rabbi Yosei holds by an inclusive prohibition, the mishna came to teach only an expanded prohibition. If you ask: why does it not teach his wife’s sister simultaneously, as where Jacob married [the man’s daughter, who would be] a half-sister of Dinah’s daughter, and [Dinah] then bore that daughter, so that she is at once his daughter’s daughter and his wife’s sister: one may say that, of prohibitions that come through betrothal, it counts only one that takes effect at the moment of betrothal, while here no prohibition existed when Jacob married until Dinah gave birth. If you ask: from where does the Gemara know that he concedes with regard to an expanded prohibition? Perhaps the whole mishna speaks of simultaneous prohibitions, as where she was betrothed under the age of three, so that at the end of her third year all the prohibitions take effect at once: one may say that it does not count a prohibition that comes through betrothal unless it takes effect at the time of betrothal, and here none took effect until the end of three years and one day; and further, that the mishna comes to teach only an expanded prohibition, as explained. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.dh: הבא על בת בתו חייב עליה משום בת בתו וכלתו
notes.he: כגון שנשאה בנו שמותר לישא בת אחותו והיא כלתו:
notes.en: [A printer’s marker at the start reads: “Up to here belongs to 14a.”] One who has intercourse with his daughter’s daughter is liable for her on account of his daughter’s daughter and his daughter-in-law: for example, where his son married her, since one is permitted to marry one’s sister’s daughter, and she is his daughter-in-law.

notes.he: כגון שהיה לבעל בת מאשה אחרת ונשאה חמיו [והוליד ממנה בת] וכשבא זה על בת בתו היתה אחות אשתו ואם נשאה אחיו קודם לכן ומת ואח"כ נשאה אחי אביו ומת ואח"כ היתה אשת איש ונדה ואח"כ בא עליה זה חייב עליה משום בת בתו וכלתו כו':
notes.en: And his wife’s sister: for example, where the husband had a daughter from another wife, and his father-in-law married her [and fathered a daughter from her], and when this man had intercourse with his daughter’s daughter, she was his wife’s sister. And if his brother married her before that and died, and afterward his father’s brother married her and died, and afterward she was a married woman and menstruating, and afterward this man had intercourse with her, he is liable for her on account of his daughter’s daughter, his daughter-in-law, and so on.

messages.text: If the elder, i.e., the man’s father, who is the woman’s great-grandfather, transgressed and married her, the man would also be liable for engaging in intercourse with her due to the prohibition of intercourse with the wife of his father.

notes.he: אביו של זה ונשאה ואחר כך בא עליה זה חייב אף על אשת האב:
notes.en: If the elder transgressed: this man’s father married her, and afterward this man had intercourse with her; he is liable also on account of a father’s wife.

notes.he: היינו אשת אחיו מאמו דאי מאביו היאך נשאה זקן ולא תפסי בה קידושין דהויא כלתו ומכאן משמע דאשת אחיו מאמו בכרת ומחייב עליה חטאת והא דממעט בתורת כהנים היינו מעריריות אבל כרת איכא:
notes.en: The wife of his brother: that is, the wife of his brother from his mother; for if from his father, how did the elder marry her? Betrothal would not take hold of her, since she is his daughter-in-law. From here it is implied that the wife of one’s maternal brother carries karet and one is liable to a sin offering for her; and what is excluded in Torat Kohanim is [only] from [the punishment of] childlessness, but there is karet.

notes.dh: ר' יוסי אמר אם עבר הזקן ונשאה
notes.he: לבת בת בנו ואח"כ בא בנו עליה חייב עליה משום אשת אב אע"ג דלא היה לאביו אישות בה אלא נשאה בעבירה הואיל ואינה אסורה לו מדאורייתא דהויא שנייה חייב עליה משום אשת אב:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei says: If the elder transgressed and married her, his son’s daughter’s daughter, and afterward his son had intercourse with her, he is liable for her on account of a father’s wife. Even though his father had no marriage with her but married her in transgression, since she is not forbidden to him by Torah law, being a secondary relative, he is liable for her on account of a father’s wife.

messages.text: And likewise, it is possible for one who engages in intercourse with the daughter of his wife to be liable to bring six sin offerings, similar to one who engages in intercourse with his own daughter, for violating the prohibitions against engaging in intercourse with his wife’s daughter, his sister, the wife of his brother, the wife of his father’s brother, a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

notes.he: חייב עליה משום בת אשתו וכלתו ואשת אחיו כו' וכן בת אשתו חייב עליה משום כל אלה:
notes.en: And likewise his wife’s daughter: he is liable for her on account of his wife’s daughter, his daughter-in-law, his brother’s wife, and so on. And likewise his wife’s daughter: he is liable for her on account of all of these.

messages.text: And it is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his wife’s daughter’s daughter to be liable to bring seven sin offerings, similar to one who engages in intercourse with his own daughter’s daughter, for violating the following prohibitions: Engaging in intercourse with his wife’s daughter’s daughter, his daughter-in-law, the wife of his brother, the wife of his father’s brother, his wife’s sister, a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

notes.he: חייב עליה בכל הללו שמות משום בת אשתו וכלתו ואחות אשתו כו' כגון שהיתה לבת אשתו אחות מאם אחרת ונשאה בעל אמה ואשת אחיו כגון שנשאה אחיו אחר מיתת בנו ואח"כ אחי אביו כו' וכן הבא על בת בת אשתו חייב עליה משום בת בת אשתו ובכל השמות הללו. וה"ה בבא על בת בנה שיש בה כל השמות הללו אלא תנא בת בתו וה"ה לבת בנה:
notes.en: And likewise one who has intercourse with his wife’s daughter is liable for her in all these categories: on account of his wife’s daughter, his daughter-in-law, his wife’s sister, and so on; [his wife’s sister] for example where his wife’s daughter had a sister from another mother, and her mother’s husband married her; and his brother’s wife, for example where his brother married her after his son’s death, and afterward his father’s brother, and so on. And likewise one who has intercourse with his wife’s daughter’s daughter is liable for her on account of his wife’s daughter’s daughter and all these categories. And the same applies to one who has intercourse with her son’s daughter, in whom all these categories are found; but it teaches the daughter’s daughter, and the same applies to the son’s daughter.

messages.text: Gemara

It is taught in the mishna that Rabbi Yosei says: If the elder, i.e., the man’s father, who is the woman’s great-grandfather, transgressed and married her, the man would also be liable for engaging in intercourse with her due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with the wife of his father. Is she permitted to marry the man’s father? She had already been married to the man’s father’s brother, and therefore even if she was widowed or divorced from him, marriage would not even take effect with the man’s father, to whom she is forbidden as the wife of his brother.
messages.quote: transgressed and married her … the wife of his father

notes.he: לאביו של זה והא אשת אחיו היא דהא מחייבינן ליה לבנו משום אשת אחי אביו אלמא אסירא ליה לאביו משום אשת אח ואין לו אישות בה ואמאי קאמר רבי יוסי חייב עליה משום אשת אב:
notes.en: Gemara. Is she permitted to him: to this man’s father? But she is his brother’s wife, for we hold his son liable on account of the wife of his father’s brother; evidently she is forbidden to his father as a brother’s wife, and he has no marriage with her. So why does Rabbi Yosei say he is liable for her on account of a father’s wife?

notes.he: לזקן מי אית ליה קדושין בגוה דליחייב בנו עלה משום אשת אב:
notes.en: Is she permitted to him: does the elder have betrothal with her, so that his son should be liable for her on account of a father’s wife?

messages.text: The marriage can take effect in a case where she happened to become designated to him for levirate marriage, when his brother died without children.
messages.quote: Is she permitted to marry the man’s father?

notes.he: מאחיו שמת בלא בנים ובא הוא ליבמה:
notes.en: Where she happened to come before him for levirate marriage: from his brother who died without sons, and he came to take her in levirate marriage.

notes.dh: אין אמר ר' יוחנן כגון שנפלה לו בייבום
notes.he: שבת בת בנו היתה נשואה לאחיו של זקן ונפלה לו בייבום:
notes.en: Yes; Rabbi Yoḥanan said: for example, where she happened to come before him for levirate marriage, since his son’s daughter’s daughter was married to the elder’s brother and came before him for levirate marriage.

messages.text: If so, that they were married legitimately through levirate marriage, what is the reason for Rabbi Yosei’s statement that he transgressed and married her?

notes.he: זקן הא שפיר עבד דאינה אסורה עליו משום איסור ערוה. ואם תאמר כלתו היא דהא מחייבינן לבריה משום אשת אח לאו פירכא היא דאיכא לאוקומה דאשת אחיו של בנו מאמו היא ולאו כלתו של אב היא אלא אשת חורגו ומותרת לו:
notes.en: If so, what is “transgressed”: the elder acted properly, since she is not forbidden to him by a prohibition of forbidden relations. And if you say: she is his daughter-in-law, for we hold his son liable on account of a brother’s wife, that is no refutation, for one can establish that she was the wife of his son’s brother from his mother, so that she is not the father’s daughter-in-law but the wife of his stepson, and she is permitted to him.

notes.he: אי הכי אם נפלה לו בייבום דמן התורה זקוקה לו דאינה מן העריות גופן מאי עבר דקאמר:
notes.en: If so, if she came before him for levirate marriage, since by Torah law she is bound to him, as she is not one of the forbidden relations themselves, what is meant by “transgressed”?

messages.text: It means that he transgressed by marrying her due to her status as his son’s daughter-in-law, which renders her a secondary relative, forbidden to him by rabbinic law, albeit not by Torah law. Consequently, it was prohibited for him to enter into the levirate marriage.

notes.dh: דעבר משום כלת בנו שהיא שניה
notes.he: מדברי סופרים דהא חייבנו לבריה משום כלתו. והוא הדין נמי דמצי לתרוצי דעבר משום בת בת בנו שהיא שניה אלא חדא מינייהו נקט:
notes.en: That he transgressed on account of his son’s daughter-in-law, who is a secondary relative: by rabbinic law, for we held his son liable on account of [her being] his daughter-in-law. The same is true that he could have answered that he transgressed on account of his son’s daughter’s daughter, who is a secondary relative, but he took one of them.

notes.he: ות"ק הואיל ואיסורא דרבנן איכא לא חשיב ליה:
notes.en: That he transgressed on account of his son’s daughter-in-law, a secondary relative: and the first tanna, since it is a rabbinic prohibition, does not count it.

notes.dh: אין שעבר על דברי חכמים דנשא שניה
notes.he: דכלת בנו הויא שניה וכן נמי בת בת בנו אלא תנא כלת בנו וה"ה לבת בת בנו:
notes.en: Yes, that he transgressed the words of the Sages, since he married a secondary relative: for his son’s daughter-in-law is a secondary relative, and so too his son’s daughter’s daughter; but it teaches his son’s daughter-in-law, and the same applies to his son’s daughter’s daughter.

messages.text: One’s daughter-in-law is a forbidden relative by Torah law, and his son’s daughter-in-law is a secondary relative, prohibited to him by rabbinic law, and similarly, you find with regard to the daughter of his son, who is prohibited to him by Torah law, and with regard to the daughter of his son’s son, until the end of all generations; the daughter of his son’s son, or of his son’s grandson, etc. They are all secondary relatives, prohibited to him by rabbinic law.
messages.lead: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: וכן אתה מוצא עד סוף כל הדורות דבת בן בנו ובת בת בנו עד סוף כל הדורות כולן הויין שניות:
notes.en: And so you find until the end of all generations: for his son’s son’s daughter and his son’s daughter’s daughter, until the end of all generations, are all secondary relatives.

messages.text: And is Rabbi Yosei of the opinion that a prohibition takes effect where another prohibition already exists? But didn’t we learn in a mishna (Sanhedrin 81a):

notes.dh: מי אית ליה לר' יוסי איסור חל על איסור
notes.he: דקתני אם עבר הזקן ונשאה חייב עליה משום אשת אב. והתנן עבר עבירה כו':
notes.en: Does Rabbi Yosei hold that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition, since it teaches: if the elder transgressed and married her, he is liable for her on account of a father’s wife? But we learned: one who committed a transgression, and so on.

messages.text: If one violated a transgression that renders him liable to two death penalties, he is sentenced to the harsher one.

notes.he: חמותו ואשת איש איכא שריפה וחנק ושריפה חמורה מחנק:
notes.en: Two death penalties: his mother-in-law and a married woman, where there is burning and strangulation, and burning is more severe than strangulation.

messages.text: He is sentenced according to the first prohibition that applied to him.

notes.he: ולא באחרונה דאין איסור חל על איסור:
notes.en: By the first prohibition: and not by the last, since a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition.

messages.text: In what case did Rabbi Yosei say that he is sentenced according to the first prohibition that applied to him? If his mother-in-law was widowed or divorced, and therefore forbidden to him only due to her status as his mother-in-law, and later she married and became forbidden as a married woman, and he engaged in intercourse with her, then he is sentenced to death by burning due to his violation of the prohibition proscribing intercourse with his mother-in-law, as this was the first prohibition to take effect.

By contrast, if she was a married woman, and then he married her daughter and she thereby became his mother-in-law, and he subsequently engaged in intercourse with her, he is sentenced to death by strangulation due to his violation of the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a married woman, despite the fact that burning is considered the more severe death penalty.
This proves that Rabbi Yosei maintains that a prohibition does not take effect where another prohibition already exists.

Rabbi Yosei concedes that in the case of an expanded prohibition it takes effect even when another prohibition already exists. Consequently, he maintains in the mishna that the prohibition against intercourse with the wife of his father applies in addition to the previously existing prohibitions.

notes.he: במתני' דאיכא איסור מוסיף ה"ה לכולל ובת אחת כדמפרש לקמן הלכך חמותו ונעשית אשת איש אף על גב דאיכא איסור מוסיף דאיתוסף איסורא דאשת איש אכולי עלמא אפ"ה נידון בחמותו משום דחמורה היא אבל אשת איש ונעשית חמותו ליכא לא כולל ולא מוסיף:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei concedes: in our mishna, where there is an expanded prohibition; the same applies to an inclusive prohibition and to a simultaneous one, as is explained below. Therefore, in the case of his mother-in-law who became a married woman, even though there is an expanded prohibition, since the prohibition of a married woman was added for everyone, even so he is judged on account of his mother-in-law, since it is more severe. But in the case of a married woman who became his mother-in-law, there is neither inclusive nor expanded.

notes.he: שאיסור חמור חל על איסור הקל או באיסורין שוין כגון איסור אח ואיסור אחות אשה אבל קל על חמור. לא חיילא אפי' באיסור מוסיף הילכך חמותו ונעשית אשת איש כו' ור' יוסי דאתא לאוספי באשת אב אינו מודה בהני דהזכיר הת"ק דבשלמא כלתו דבסקילה חייל אבת בתו דבשריפה ואשת אב חייל אכלתו דשניהן שוין אבל אשת איש דבחנק לא חיילא אשריפה ואסקילה וכ"ש אחות אשה ואשת אח ואשת אחי אביו ונדה דחייבי כריתות גרידי לא חיילי הילכך לר' יוסי לא משכחת אלא ג' בת בתו כלתו ואשת אב:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei concedes with regard to an expanded prohibition: where a severe prohibition takes effect on a lighter prohibition, or with equal prohibitions, such as the prohibition of a brother[’s wife] and the prohibition of a wife’s sister; but a light one does not take effect on a severe one, even as an expanded prohibition. Therefore, his mother-in-law who became a married woman, and so on. And Rabbi Yosei, who comes to add the father’s wife, does not concede those that the first tanna mentioned. Granted, his daughter-in-law, [punished] by stoning, takes effect on his daughter’s daughter, [punished] by burning; and the father’s wife takes effect on his daughter-in-law, since the two are equal. But a married woman, [punished] by strangulation, does not take effect on burning and stoning; and all the more so a wife’s sister, a brother’s wife, the wife of his father’s brother and a menstruating woman, which carry mere karet, do not take effect. Therefore, according to Rabbi Yosei you find only three: his daughter’s daughter, his daughter-in-law and his father’s wife.

notes.he: פירש"י דה"ה באיסור כולל ולא משמע הכי בפרק ד' אחין:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei concedes with regard to an expanded prohibition: Rashi explained that the same applies to an inclusive prohibition, but this does not seem so from the chapter Arba’a Aḥin [in Yevamot].

notes.dh: א"ר אבהו מודה ר' יוסי באיסור מוסיף
notes.he: היכא דנתוספו אחרים על איסורו דהתם איסור חל על איסור. ואי אמרת חמותו ונעשית אשת איש הא איתוסף הכא איסורא לגבי אחר לכולי עלמא וליחייב הכי שתים אין ודאי תרתי מיחייב אבל בתרי קטלי לא מצי קטלי ליה הלכך נידון בזיקה ראשונה והיינו דקאמר התם ביבמות מעלה עליו הכתוב כאילו עשה שתים ועשה אחת למאי נפקא מינה לקוברו בין רשעים גמורים בין נסקלין ונשרפין. אבל הכא גבי חטאות היכא דאיסור מוסיף הוא מודי ר' יוסי דחייב שתים דאיסור חל על איסור:
notes.en: Rabbi Abbahu said: Rabbi Yosei concedes with regard to an expanded prohibition, where others were added to his prohibition, for there a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition. And if you say: his mother-in-law who became a married woman; here a prohibition was added with regard to another, with regard to everyone, so let him be liable to two in this way? Yes, certainly he is liable to two, but he cannot be executed with two executions; therefore he is judged by the first prohibition. And this is what it says there in Yevamot: the verse ascribes to him as though he did two, and he did one. What difference does it make? To bury him among the completely wicked, among those stoned and burned. But here, with regard to sin offerings, where there is an expanded prohibition, Rabbi Yosei concedes that he is liable to two, since a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition.

messages.text: Rabbi Yosei concedes with regard to an expanded prohibition.
messages.lead: And similarly, when Ravin came from Eretz Yisrael he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

messages.text: What expanded prohibition is there here?

notes.he: והכא בבת בתו ועבר אביו ונשאה מאי איסור מוסיף איכא - דליתוסף איסור אשת אב אהאי:
notes.en: And here, in the case of his daughter’s daughter where his father transgressed and married her, what expanded prohibition is there, so that the prohibition of a father’s wife should be added for this one?

notes.he: והכא מאי איסור מוסיף איכא לגביה דהיכא דעבר הזקן ונשאה:
notes.en: And here, what expanded prohibition is there with regard to him, where the elder transgressed and married her?

messages.text: The expanded prohibition applies when there is another son of the grandfather, i.e., another son of the father of the subject of the mishna. Consequently, since a prohibition against intercourse with the woman is added with regard to his father’s other son, when his father marries this woman, another prohibition against intercourse with her is added with regard to him as well.

notes.he: ואחיו של זה הוא דמגו דאיתוסף איסורא אההוא ברא משום אשת אב איתוסף נמי אהאי:
notes.en: Where the grandfather has a son: who is this man’s brother. Since a prohibition was added for that son on account of a father’s wife, it was added for this one too.

notes.he: איכא כגון דאית ליה ברא אחריני לסבא מיגו (דאיתי) [דאיתוסף] איסורא לגביה בריה דאסור באשת אביו איתוסף נמי איסורא לגביה האי:
notes.en: There is, for example where the grandfather has another son: since a prohibition was added with regard to his son, who is forbidden his father’s wife, a prohibition was added also with regard to this one.

messages.text: Mishna

It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his mother-in-law to be liable to bring seven sin offerings for doing so, due to the unwitting violation of the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his mother-in-law, and his daughter-in-law, and the wife of his brother, and the wife of his father’s brother, and his wife’s sister, and a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

notes.dh: הבא על בת בתו כו' משום חמותו וכלתו
notes.he: כגון שחמותו נשואה לבנו. ואחות אשתו כגון שהיה נשוי קודם לכן אחות חמותו ואשת אחיו כגון שמת בנו ונשאה אחיו ואח"כ נשאה אחי אביו ומת ואח"כ נשאה איש אחר והיא נדה וכן הבא על אם חמותו חייב עליה משום אם חמותו וכלתו ואחות אשתו וכל השמות הללו:
notes.en: One who has intercourse with his daughter’s daughter, and so on, on account of his mother-in-law and his daughter-in-law [so the lemma reads; the explanation concerns the mother-in-law]: for example, where his mother-in-law was married to his son. And his wife’s sister: for example, where he was previously married to his mother-in-law’s sister. And his brother’s wife: for example, where his son died and his brother married her, and afterward his father’s brother married her and died, and afterward another man married her, and she is menstruating. And likewise one who has intercourse with his mother-in-law’s mother is liable for her on account of his mother-in-law’s mother, his daughter-in-law, his wife’s sister and all these categories.

messages.text: And likewise, the same applies with regard to one who engages in intercourse with the mother of his father-in-law or with the mother of his mother-in-law.

notes.he: חייב עליה משום אם חמיו וכלתו ואחות אשתו כו':
notes.en: And likewise one who has intercourse with his father-in-law’s mother is liable for her on account of his father-in-law’s mother, his daughter-in-law, his wife’s sister, and so on.

messages.text: It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his mother-in-law to be liable due to the unwitting violation of the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his mother-in-law, and the mother of his mother-in-law, and the mother of his father-in-law.

notes.dh: מתני' ר' יוחנן בן נורי אומר כו' משום חמותו ואם חמותו
notes.he: שהיה נשוי בתה ובת בתה ואם חמיו שנשא את בת בנה:
notes.en: Mishna. Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says, and so on: on account of his mother-in-law and his mother-in-law’s mother, where he was married to her daughter and to her daughter’s daughter; and his father-in-law’s mother, where he married her son’s daughter.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri Those three prohibitions are all one category of prohibition, derived from the same verse: “You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter; you shall not take her son’s daughter, or her daughter’s daughter” (Leviticus 18:17). Consequently, one is not liable to bring separate sin offerings for violating these prohibitions.

verse.he: עֶרְוַת אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ לֹא תְגַלֵּה אֶת־בַּת־בְּנָהּ וְאֶת־בַּת־בִּתָּהּ לֹא תִקַּח לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ שַׁאֲרָה הֵנָּה זִמָּה הִוא׃
verse.en: Do not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter; nor shall you take to wife her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter and uncover her nakedness: they are kindred; it is depravity.

notes.he: בחד קרא כתיבי ובחד לאו הלכך אין חילוק חטאות ביניהם:
notes.en: The three of them are one category: they are written in one verse and in one prohibition; therefore there is no division of sin offerings between them.

notes.dh: ר' יוחנן בן נורי אמר הבא על חמותו חייב עליה משום חמותו ואם חמותו ואם חמיו
notes.he: כיצד כגון שהיתה לחמותו שתי בנות ובן אחד ונשא הוא הבת האחת ונשא בת אחיה ובת אחותה וכשבא על חמותו הזקנה הרי היא חמותו ואם חמותו ואם חמיו אמרו לו שלשתן שם אחד הן. שם חמות ואינו חייב אלא חטאת אחת:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said: One who has intercourse with his mother-in-law is liable for her on account of his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law’s mother and his father-in-law’s mother. How so? For example, where his mother-in-law had two daughters and one son, and he married one daughter, and married her brother’s daughter and her sister’s daughter; when he has intercourse with the elderly mother-in-law, she is his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law’s mother and his father-in-law’s mother. They said to him: The three of them are one category, the category of mother-in-law, and he is liable to only one sin offering.

messages.text: Gemara
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Sumakhos said the same thing.

With regard to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, this is referring to that which we stated in the mishna. With regard to Sumakhos, what is the equivalent ruling that he stated? It is the following ruling, as we learned in a mishna (Ḥullin 82a):
messages.quote: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Sumakhos said the same thing

messages.text: Continues on 15a with that mishna: one who slaughtered an animal and its daughter’s daughter, and afterward slaughtered its daughter, incurs forty lashes; Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir that he incurs eighty.
